smell_validity.evidence: The base kept the raw-to-date policy in one place; the injection splits it across per-part view modules — including two month implementations (input and select shapes) that must agree — and makes the day view depend on a sibling's month rule. One policy now evolves only through coordinated multi-module edits. Per-part locality still reads arguably natural, so the cost is clear but not instantly unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every codec tweak now repeats in several components; the select month variant participates only via runtime dispatch, so a fallback change can silently miss locales that render selects. Adding a part or shape touches views, three tables and the dispatch. The two January rules must stay in agreement, and the day bound is entangled with the month rule; consolidation restores a single ownership boundary within this component.

development_plausibility.evidence: Helpers sit beside their JSX with repository-style doc comments, the select's NaN guard matches a non-numeric placeholder, the day view reuses the nearest sibling decode, and the part tables extend the base's existing valueAsNumber element walk — credible incremental growth. Mild artificiality remains: the three parallel strategy tables and uniform encoder pairs read slightly task-shaped rather than fully organic.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt fixes problem, finished state and preservation boundary together: enumerated fallback semantics per configuration (current year, January placeholder, 1st of month), month-length clamping, native path, unchanged API and unmodified specs. The runtime-flow warning plus the explicit ban on per-shape copies materially blocks the realistic near-miss — leaving the select decoder unconsolidated — and wrong defaults, while leaving implementation choice open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Consolidation spans distinct purposes: per-part decoding whose fallbacks differ (first-of-month, January, live-clock year), select-shaped decoding with NaN semantics, value-to-text encoding, runtime select-versus-input resolution, and the day bound reusing the month rule. At least two purposes need genuinely different decisions, while encoding stays near-uniform, so not 5.

localization_burden.evidence: DateInput's tables and imports enumerate fragments, but the select decoder is live only via part-keyed registration plus the runtime element-shape dispatch, so deciding its status combines coordinator and view behavior; the day view's month consumption surfaces only by tracing a sibling import. Codec-adjacent lookalikes (native input path, shared clamping helpers) must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: The month rule is shared by candidate composition and the day-view bound, so a one-sided change to the human-month/index conversion makes the submitted month and clamp bound disagree; both January implementations must move together with the dispatch selecting between them. Beyond these shared rules, orphaned imports fail compilation, which bounds coordination.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform relocation — moving every module-scope part helper into a shared module and re-importing verbatim — clears roughly two-thirds of the spread (four view restatements plus the day bound's import) with no per-location behavioral decision. Remaining are the input/select month duplication, a real shared-policy decision, and the coordinator's three restated part tables.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Plausible mis-consolidations — a month-index change applied at only one of its two consumers, or a dropped select fallback — yield ordinary wrong onChange values or clamping that the untouched per-part specs would assert. But hoisting the current-year default to module scope compiles and passes until a session crosses New Year — a special-state stale-year failure with no time-crossing coverage indicated.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
